text: The city council will vote December 8, 2026 on a Flock Safety contract for license plate reader cameras.
The proposed police budget adds $50,000 for ALPR camera maintenance.
House Bill 500 would limit how long license plate reader data may be retained.
The chief told the council the real-time crime center needs the plate reader cameras to stay online.
During public comment, nine speakers opposed the surveillance camera contract and two speakers supported it.
The parks department will renovate the picnic pavilion and replace two grills.
A restaurant on Main Street requested a zoning variance for outdoor seating.
A flock of geese settled on the lake behind city hall after the storm.
The library summer reading program begins June 1 and is open to all ages.
Public works opened bids to resurface three miles of Oak Street.
